note: The Central Bank of Seychelles' comparison of every bank's charges (applicable 1 October to 31 December 2026) was read for every bank that offers a credit card: Absa Bank Seychelles, the Mauritius Commercial Bank (Seychelles), Nouvobanq and Al Salam Bank; the Seychelles Commercial Bank, the Credit Union, Bank of Baroda and Bank of Ceylon offer none. Absa: its Classic, Platinum and Signature credit cards cost 100, 500 and 1,000 rupees a year, bear 33% a year on the unpaid balance, 2% on a cash withdrawal, 5% on spending in a foreign currency, a late fee of 10% of the past-due amount (at least 100 rupees, written as a share of the unpaid part) and an over-limit fee of 6% of the excess (at least 100); its subscription or issue fee row repeats each card's yearly figure, read as the same fee and not written twice. The MCB: its VISA Classic and VISA Gold cost 100 and 400 rupees a year for the primary card, bear 16% a year on the unpaid balance, 2% on a cash withdrawal (at least 50 rupees), 5% on foreign currency spending, and 50 rupees each for a late payment and for exceeding the limit. Nouvobanq: its VISA Gold card costs 1,000 rupees to issue and 250 a year, with 'no charge' as its interest on the unpaid balance, read as a card settled in full, and 5% on a cash withdrawal; its Signature card costs 500 to issue, bears 15% a year, and 100 rupees each for a cash withdrawal, a late payment and exceeding the limit; the Gold card's 'bonus fee' (up to 2% when unsecured) doesn't say of what and isn't written. Al Salam Bank's credit card, its only one (the table names it no further), costs 500 rupees a year, 1.5% a month on the balance, 3% on a cash withdrawal (at least 300 rupees), 500 rupees for a late payment and 250 for exceeding the limit. Business and corporate cards aren't written.
